Stable Engine Last updated: 2026-11-18 Automate the engine through the C ABI: build scenes, add components, write materials, generate terrain and water, and render RGBA images offscreen with no window. Everything Doppio does to the engine goes through one C ABI, libcaffeine-capi ( include/caffeine/capi/EngineAPI.h , CAFFEINE_CAPI_VERSION 8). Anything the editor can do, a script can do: create entities, add components, write materials, generate terrain and water, move the camera and render the scene to RGBA pixels, offscreen, with no window . This page is for automating that: test scenes, generated images, thumbnails, regression pictures, batch renders. The shape of the API # Idea What it means Session caffeine_session_create() makes one scene (its own ECS world). Everything else takes the session. Destroy it with caffeine_session_destroy . Entities uint32_t ids. caffeine_session_create_entity(session, name) returns CAFFEINE_ENTITY_NONE on failure. Transforms are position, rotation (Euler degrees) and scale. Parent with caffeine_session_set_entity_parent . Components by name Components are described at run time. List them with caffeine_component_type_count/at , their fields with caffeine_component_type_field_at , add one with caffeine_session_add_component(session, entity, type_id) and set a field with caffeine_session_entity_component_field_set . Field kinds: f32, bool, i32, u32, vec2/3/4, string, enum (by option index), colour. This is the same reflection the editor Inspector uses, so a new component shows up here without an API change. Assets caffeine_session_set_asset_root(session, folder) sets the project folder. Reference Last updated: 2026-11-18 The reflection registry that exposes every engine component to Lua, Dryad, the Inspector and the C ABI. Every component the engine can describe is scriptable, in Lua and in Dryad , through one shared reflection registry ( src/caffeine/scene/ComponentReflection.* ). The editor inspector, the C ABI and both languages read the same table, so a component registered once is available everywhere, with its fields, ranges and enum options. ComponentAccess.* is the language-neutral layer the scripting hosts use. Component and field names are matched case-insensitively and ignoring spaces, _ and - : "Rigid Body 3D" , "rigidbody3d" and "rigid_body_3d" are the same component. VolumetricMixer ( src/caffeine/audio/volumetric/ ) is separate from AudioService : a game that wants plain 2D or 3D sound keeps using that. The mixer needs no sound card. It renders blocks of stereo samples, so the same code feeds a device in play, a WAV file in a test and a video in the demos. 1. What a voice goes through # Stage What it does Propagation The clip is read at t - distance / c , so a shot 150 m away is heard 0.44 s late. A moving source changes that delay continuously, which is the Doppler shift: exact, with no pitch trick ( dopplerScale 0 freezes it) Distance Inverse law gain (half for every doubling) and air absorption: the cutoff falls with distance, so near sound is clear and far sound is dull Occlusion The segment source to listener is traced through the AcousticWorld . What a wall lets through is quiet and dull: lows pass walls far better than highs, and thicker walls keep less Diffraction If the sound can bend round the obstacle (the end of a wall, a doorway) that path is mixed in too, quieter and duller with the extra distance, and the voice is heard coming from the opening The room 31 rays round the listener (up to 300 m) give its size, openness, sky exposure and reflectivity. A feedback delay network (8 lines) fits the reverb tail and level to them, and far hard surfaces send back distinct echoes at 2 d / c . Overview # The Job System distributes heavy work (physics, AI, animation, asset loading) across CPU cores. Each job is a lightweight unit of work executed by a worker thread . Approach: thread pool with work-stealing — each worker has local deques; when they are empty, it steals from another worker. This provides load balancing without central coordination. Implemented today: Three priority levels: Critical / Normal / Background Per-worker deques per priority level, plus global queues per priority JobHandle completion tracking with slot index + version JobBarrier for waiting on a group of jobs scheduleParallelFor chunking Not implemented yet: fibers. A job runs to completion on an OS thread; it cannot suspend halfway without blocking that thread. Stable Doppio Last updated: 2026-11-21 Clouds that shade the ground, height fog, rain with depth, wind and lightning with thunder as one system that agrees with the sun and with Photon's GI, and the Environment tab that manages it. The scene's weather lives in two reflected components on one entity: Volumetric Clouds (the sky) and Weather (fog, rain, wind, lightning and the coupling between everything). Doppio edits them from the Environment tab (View menu, next to Photon) and from the Inspector: both write the same fields, so they never disagree, and scripts and agents use the same fields too. The Environment tab: presets, clouds, fog, rain and the link between them 1. Reference Engine Last updated: 2026-11-21 Source: micromeshes.md A mesh is cut into clusters of at most 128 triangles and a hierarchy of simplified levels. Each frame a compute pass picks the coarsest cut whose error is invisible and one draw renders it, now through the lit scene renderer and its G-buffer. This page shows what exists, with renders from the real GPU path, and what is still missing. Micromeshes are our own design (see graphics-roadmap.md for the plan and the review of the original proposal). Everything on this page is implemented and tested except the items under What is missing . 1. What you are looking at # One rock of 81 920 triangles, four error budgets. Every colour patch is one cluster (at most 128 triangles). The counts are the clusters that survive the frustum and back-face tests, so the exact cut shows only the half that faces the camera. The coarser cuts use bigger flat clusters made from merged and simplified groups. The same error budget while the camera pulls away and returns: the GPU picks a coarser cut by itself, and the triangle counter in the corner follows. Frames are rendered by MicromeshGpu : the cull compute pass, then one drawIndexedIndirect over every cluster. 2. In the scene: the lit G-buffer draw # Turn on Micromesh in a Mesh Renderer (the Inspector shows it with its Micromesh error (px) ; scripts and scenes see the same two fields) and the scene renderer draws that mesh as a cluster cut instead of a plain mesh: same lit shader ( scene_lit.frag ), same G-buffer, so Photon, SSAO and TAA need nothing new. The real scene renderer (the lit shader, the G-buffer, the sun's shadow cascades): 81 rocks of 81 408 triangles each, 6.6 million triangles in the scene. Stable Doppio Last updated: 2026-11-21 Indirect light, colour bleeding and sky occlusion without ray-tracing hardware, and the Photon tab that manages it. Photon is the engine's global illumination (GI). Doppio edits it from the Photon tab (View menu, next to the generators) and from the Photon GI component in the Inspector: both write the same fields, so they never disagree. The Photon tab: lighting, voxel geometry, debug view and the live voxel statistics 1. How Photon works # Part What it does Near field Screen-anchored radiance cascades (K to 0) traced against the depth buffer, merged front to back and resolved to SH-L1 probes ( photon_cascade.comp , photon_c0.comp ) Far field Four clipmap levels of voxels (cells of 0.25, 0.5, 1 and 2 m, 64 cubed each) with a lattice of probes per level; rays that leave the screen query it Material volume The albedo and coverage of the scene's surfaces, written by the triangle voxeliser ( photon_voxelize_tri.comp ) and by the screened fill Injection The sun, point and spot lights, and the sky, are injected into the voxel faces with a shadow marched through the material volume ( photon_inject.comp ) Feedback The previous frame's irradiance is fed back with a cap and a reprojected history, which is the multi-bounce Temporal average Every probe offsets its traced directions by its own fixed amount, so the noise is not coherent; the resolve averages the reprojected irradiance of the previous frame into this one (weight 0.4 while the scene changes, 0.07 when still, quicker for large differences), and the far probes follow the same weight The screen cascades dominate what the camera sees. Slow frames were being guessed at. The profiler gives the numbers: every stage of the renderer is a scope, and the Profiler tab (View menu) shows them as a tree with the average, the worst case and how many times each ran. The Profiler tab: the frame time, the two controls and the scope tree with a bar per scope 1. What it times # The engine has one process-wide tree of scopes ( Debug::Profiler ). The renderer opens a scope for each stage: gathering the scene, the shadows, the opaque and translucent passes, reflections, Photon's passes one by one, and the post-processing stack. Mode What a scope's time is CPU scopes (default) The time the CPU spent recording that stage. The GPU runs behind it, so this is not the GPU's cost GPU timing The time the stage really takes: the GPU passes wait for the GPU at their edges, so the scope covers recording plus execution SDL3 GPU has no portable timestamp queries, so GPU timing works by submitting what has been recorded and waiting for it at the start and the end of each GPU scope ( CF_GPU_SCOPE ). That serialises the CPU and the GPU: frames get slower while it is on . It is a measuring mode, off by default. A scope inside a render pass (the per-mesh and terrain scopes) cannot wait, so it always shows CPU time. 2. Where they live | What is not here yet

Textures and materials are generated, so the baked PNG is not the only product: the same material can react to the world without re-baking its maps . A modifier is a few numbers the shader applies on top of the material, so a script can wet a rock when it rains, cover a roof with snow or age a wall. Modifier Range Effect Tint colour, white = none multiplies the albedo (season shift, team colour) Wetness 0 dry .. 1 soaked darker albedo and a glossy film (low roughness) Snow 0 none .. 1 everything facing up white, rough cover on upward faces; the more snow, the further down the slopes it reaches Age 0 new .. 1 old washed-out, darker, rougher Where they live # In the material ( .mat keys mod_tint , mod_wetness , mod_snow , mod_age ; MaterialSurface , C ABI v10 , the Material panel's Run-time modifiers section): the defaults a material ships with. On the entity (Mesh Renderer fields Tint , Wetness , Snow , Age , saved with the scene): the values a game changes at run time. They are ordinary reflected fields, so scripts read and write them like any other ( Mesh Renderer , Wetness , 0..1), and so do the Inspector and the agent bridge. The renderer combines both: tints multiply, the amounts add and clamp to 0..1. Entities that share one material and one mesh still batch only when their modifiers are equal. Scenes saved before the fields existed load with neutral modifiers. What is not here yet # Modifiers that need new maps (damage decals, moss growing in cracks) still need the generator's graph at run time; the graph and its parameter schema are not shipped with the baked output yet. Foliage wind and translucency ( wind_* , translucency ) are material-only, not per entity.

Reference Engine Last verified: 2026-11-18 Source: ecs/World.hpp Caffeine is an archetype ECS: entities are numeric ids, components are plain structs, and every entity with the same component set shares one dense archetype that queries can walk linearly. Table of Contents # Introduction Architecture Overview Components Entities Queries Systems Command Buffer Performance API Reference Common Patterns Troubleshooting Introduction # The ECS stores game state as data and runs behaviour in systems. An entity is a u32 id plus a World* ; a component is a plain struct registered by type; a system is an object with onUpdate(World&, f32) . Why ECS? # Traditional object-oriented game code puts state and behaviour in deep class hierarchies. That makes behaviour hard to combine, scatters related data across memory and makes safe parallel iteration difficult. The Caffeine ECS composes instead: Components hold data only ( Position2D , Velocity2D , Health , your own structs). Entities are ids that group components; they have no data of their own. Queries select every entity with a component signature. Systems receive the matching components and mutate them. Result: contiguous component arrays, cheap archetype matching and a clear place for each piece of logic. Design goals # Fast query iteration over dense component arrays. Structural changes are explicit ( add , remove , destroy ) and never hidden in a getter. Parallel iteration is opt-in and does not require locks around component storage. No global system registry: the host decides which systems run and in what order. The correctness suite lives in tests/test_phase2_3.cpp ; measure frame budgets on your own scene rather than relying on a fixed number. Stable Engine Last verified: 2026-11-18 Source: ecs/World.hpp Caffeine uses an archetype-based ECS: entities with the same component set live in contiguous storage, and queries iterate matching archetypes instead of scanning every entity. Concepts # Term Meaning Entity A u32 id plus a World* . No data, no logic, no virtuals. Component A plain struct registered by type; no methods, no base class. Archetype The set of entities with an identical ComponentSet ; component arrays are contiguous by type. Query A ComponentQuery describing required, excluded and any-of components. World Owns entities, archetypes and the component storage. System An object with onUpdate(World&, f32) ; the engine or game calls it. Entity # cpp Copy Caffeine::ECS::Entity entity = world. create ( "Player" ); entity. id (); // u32 entity. isValid (); // id != u32_max entity. add <Position3D>({ 0 , 1 , 0 }); entity. has <Position3D>(); entity. get <Position3D>(); entity. getOrAdd <Health>( 100 ); entity. remove <Health>(); entity. destroy (); Entity::INVALID is the default-constructed value. A destroyed entity id may be reused; stale handles are not generation-checked, so treat handles as short-lived and re-query after structural changes. Stable Engine Namespace: Caffeine::Scene Last verified: 2026-11-18 Source: scene/SceneManager.hpp The scene layer adds a parent/child hierarchy, world transforms and a scene stack on top of the ECS, plus the serializers that write a world to a .caf file. Overview # The scene layer is a handful of small pieces on top of ECS::World : Scene::Parent — the parent link used by the hierarchy. Scene::WorldTransform — the resolved matrix for each entity. Scene::EntityLayer — the inherited render layer. Scene::propagateTransforms — recomputes world matrices and inherited layers. Scene::SceneManager — a stack of worlds and a transition timer. Scene::SceneSerializer — the minimal binary/JSON scene serializer. Editor::SceneSerializer — the full project scene serializer used by Doppio, the runtime and the C ABI. Parent Stores the parent entity and a dirty flag. The flag is serialized but propagateTransforms recomputes every entity each call; it does not skip clean entries. WorldTransform One Mat4 per entity, written by propagateTransforms . Local Transform components are never rewritten by inheritance. EntityLayer A u8 layer inherited from the parent when the child has no layer of its own. Beta Engine Last updated: 2026-11-18 Real-time global illumination without hardware ray tracing: screen-anchored radiance cascades, interval merge and a sky/ambient far field. Photon is a native engine system : it is compiled into caffeine-core and used by the editor and runtime. It is not loaded as a plugin. Photon indirect lighting in the runtime Status # Photon part Status Screen-anchored near field Implemented : world-aligned cascades traced against the depth buffer, merged front to back, resolved to SH-L1 Far field Implemented : four voxel clipmap levels with probes, the whole scene's triangles voxelised (terrain, skinned and cut-out meshes included) Dirty regions Implemented : a moving object revoxelises only the boxes where it was and is Direct light into GI Implemented : sun, point and spot lights injected into the voxels, shadowed through the material volume Multi-bounce feedback Implemented : the previous irradiance is fed back with a cap and a reprojected history Bounce gain Implemented : scales the light the voxels hold Motion vectors Not yet: the history reprojects with the previous matrix Glossy reflection pass Not yet Temporal denoiser Provided by the engine's TAA: Photon runs before it The complete guide, with the Photon tab, presets, statistics and the C ABI, is Photon: global illumination in Doppio . The active Rust/Iced Doppio does not load C++ plugins. These pages document the C++/ImGui plugin SDK and its host in caffeine-runtime / doppio-archived . The engine still builds every plugin from the submodule so the SDK stays compile-tested. The engine build compiles every plugin from the doppio-plugins submodule into build/plugins/ , but the legacy C++ host does not load them until the user enables each one in its Plugin Manager. Doppio plugin architecture Plugin lifecycle Where plugins live # Plugin sources are maintained in the separate doppio-plugins repository and added to the engine as a git submodule: bash Copy ./scripts/submodules.sh The normal engine build compiles every plugin and writes the libraries to build/plugins/ : bash Copy cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release cmake --build build -j There is no second build step. CAFFEINE_BUILD_DOPPIO_PLUGINS=OFF is the only way to skip plugin compilation, for minimal/headless builds. Install # Copy the libraries into any discovered plugin directory: Scope Directory Project <project>/plugins/ Doppio build <caffeine>/build/plugins/ Next to the binary <doppio-dir>/plugins/ Enable only what you need # Open Plugins → Plugin Manager . Discovered libraries start disabled : Toggling Enabled loads the shared library immediately and calls OnLoad() . Unloading removes its panels, menu actions, component drawers and services. Frame pipeline # The pane reports its logical size. The editor keeps a desired render size in physical pixels and requests a frame at most every 16 ms. caffeine_session_render_begin(width, height) starts an offscreen engine render. The 16 ms ViewportTick polls caffeine_session_render_poll into a reusable RGBA buffer. States are Pending , Ready , Idle and Failed . On Ready , the pixels are uploaded to an Iced/wgpu texture through uikit/components/viewport_shader.rs . A content hash skips identical frames, so a static scene does not re-upload every tick. The editor draws the toolbar, HUD, gizmo and scene markers over the frame. Those overlays project with the same camera that produced the image. Warning. SDL_GPU does not expose a native texture handle through the public API. A shared wgpu texture is therefore not possible without a renderer change (wgpu backend, SDL patch or a separate window). The readback path is the supported one; do not describe it as zero-copy. Philosophy: game code never asks "was W pressed?" — it asks "was the MoveUp action activated?". Bindings map W → MoveUp , but the player can reconfigure them. The header has no SDL3 dependency . The host application translates SDL events into injectKeyDown() / injectKeyUp() / injectMouseButtonDown() / injectGamepadAxis() calls; tests feed the same injection API directly. Call beginFrame() before injecting a frame's events and endFrame() once all events have been injected. Stable Namespace: `Caffeine::Physics2D` Last verified: 2026-11-18 Source: physics/PhysicsSystem2D.hpp The 2D rigid-body system: a spatial-hash broad phase, AABB and circle collision, impulse response with friction, layers, triggers and raycasts. Overview # A simple 2D physics system with rigid-body dynamics, AABB and circle collision, layers and a simple collision response (restitution + friction). caffeine-runtime registers it next to the event bus. Intentional scope: this covers most 2D cases. For joints, CCD or convex hulls, integrate a dedicated library (Box2D/Jolt) as a scaling trigger. Behaviour (verified by tests/test_physics2d.cpp ): Fixed step. onUpdate(dt) runs whole steps of kFixedStep (1/60 s) and carries the remainder over (at most 8 steps per frame), so falls, forces and landings are the same at any frame rate. A force holds for the frame it is asked in (force x frame time); impulses are instant; a push wakes a sleeping body. Scenery. A collider with isStatic never moves, even if it carries a RigidBody2D ; a floor that is only a collider holds bodies up. A body that would move more than half its size in a slice is advanced in up to 8 slices with a collision pass each, so thin walls are not jumped over. Contacts. Circle against box has its normal from A to B in either order (a centre inside the box leaves by the nearest side). Restitution is the smaller of the two and is ignored for a speed of one step of gravity (no jitter at rest). Pairs are resolved in a fixed order, so a scene replays identically. Hierarchy. The game runs Dryad. The canvas only records how that text was built. File contract # In the project scripts folder (the same one the Lua watcher already uses): File Read by Role nome_script.dyd Dryad runtime The real program. The only thing executed. nome_script.node.json Editor only Canvas positions, node types, wires, and parameters. flowchart LR canvas[Doppio canvas] json["nome_script.node.json"] dyd["nome_script.dyd"] host[DryadHost] play[Play mode] canvas --> json canvas --> dyd dyd --> host --> play json -.-> canvas The runtime ignores the JSON. If the JSON is missing, the game still runs. If the .dyd is edited by hand, the game uses that text; the canvas may be stale until the graph is rebuilt. The emitter must be deterministic: the same graph always produces the same .dyd . Language boundary # Dryad stays a general-purpose language. Caffeine, Doppio, ECS, nodes, and .node.json do not enter the language, the standard library, or the syscalls. The Natural Fluids plugin adds animated water and real 2D/3D fluid volumes on top of the engine's fluid simulation. Natural Fluids is a plugin for the legacy C++/ImGui host for animated water and real fluids. It adds a NaturalFluidComponent to entities and four authoring levels, from a flat water plane to a 3D Eulerian fluid volume. Natural Fluids water and fire Four levels # Level What it does Flat water A flat animated water plane with a transparent, low-roughness material. Wind + physics Gerstner wind waves plus a conservative shallow-water solver: wind stress, drops, impulses, terrain bed and volume conservation. Realistic water A broad Gerstner spectrum with finite-depth dispersion, choppiness, whitecap foam and depth attenuation. Fluid volume A real 3D Stable-Fluids solver for water, fire, fog and smoke. How it works # The engine keeps the simulation, not the plugin: WaveField samples a deterministic Gerstner spectrum from wind, direction, choppiness, wavelength and depth. ShallowWater is a face-staggered shallow-water solver. It conserves volume in a closed basin and reacts to wind, drops and impulses. EulerFluid2D and FluidVolume use semi-Lagrangian advection, Jacobi pressure projection, buoyancy and vorticity confinement. Density and temperature are transported by the incompressible velocity field, so fire rises and smoke/fog drift with the real flow. The C ABI, lifecycle and host callbacks a plugin implements for the legacy C++/ImGui editor. Plugins are shared libraries that implement a small C ABI. The legacy C++ host loads them with dlopen / LoadLibrary and calls into your code through PluginHostApi function pointers. The active Rust Doppio does not load these libraries. Meshes with at least 600 indices get two clustered LODs (Rossignac vertex clustering, Assets::MeshLOD::buildClusteredLod ) in GpuSceneRenderer . The source mesh is never rewritten. Distance (world units ÷ largest entity scale) LOD < 120 original 120–350 cell = 3% of the AABB diagonal > 350 cell = 8% of the AABB diagonal The swap uses 12% hysteresis so it does not oscillate at the border. Terrain stays in TerrainLodSystem . GPU instancing exists: CommandBuffer::drawIndexedInstanced and the forward Instancing feature (on by default, up to 256 draws per batch; see forward-render-features.md ). Stable Engine Last verified: 2026-11-18 Source: rhi/RenderDevice.hpp The RHI wraps SDL3 GPU: one device, explicit command buffers, textures, buffers, shaders, samplers, graphics pipelines and compute pipelines. The engine does not call SDL_GPU directly outside this layer. Why it exists. Render code targets one API. Today it is SDL3 GPU (Vulkan, D3D12 or Metal underneath); a future backend can be swapped without rewriting the renderer. Up to three frames are in flight ( MAX_FRAMES_IN_FLIGHT ). Offscreen rendering # For thumbnails, material previews, the Doppio viewport and tests: cpp Copy CommandBuffer* cmd = device. beginOffscreen (); // record into a texture, then submit without waiting device. endOffscreen (cmd); // later: copy the texture and call device.releaseOffscreenResources() readTexture(texture, pixels) reads mip 0 of a 4-byte-per-pixel colour texture and blocks. beginOffscreen has no swapchain, so it works without a window when the device was created with initOffscreen . Reference Namespace: `Caffeine::Render` Last verified: 2026-11-18 Source: render/RenderFeatures.hpp Analytical height fog computed inside the forward shader: what each quality level costs, and what the engine still does not do (froxel volumes, god rays). Active in Forward Render Features → Volumetrics (or caffeine.forwardrender.setVolumetrics ). By default it is Off . There is no second geometry draw. The fog marches from the camera to the surface inside the already running shader: Low — 6 steps Medium — 12 steps High — 24 steps Density and Height control density and the falloff with altitude Anisotropy turns the fog towards the sun Sample shadows reads the shadow map at each step (more expensive; leave it off if the frame goes over 16 ms) A froxel volume does not exist yet, and neither do god rays. See forward-render-features.md for the component and the Lua API. A volumetric-cloud component with a non-zero mist density forces the scene fog to Low when volumetrics are otherwise off, so ground geometry sits in the same mist as the sky.

Reference Last updated: 2026-11-18 Source: src/caffeine/script One scripting surface, two languages: what Lua and Dryad can do today, what was added in this pass, and the ordered plan to grow the API without letting the two drift apart. 1. Design rules # One name, one meaning. A capability exists in both languages under parallel names: Lua caffeine.<area>.<verb> , Dryad caffeine_<area>_<verb> . Lookup tables (key, axis and action names) are shared C++ ( ScriptInputNames.hpp ), so both accept the same strings. Bindings are thin. Logic lives in engine modules; a binding validates arguments, calls it and logs errors. Natives never crash on a bad id, a missing world or an unknown name. Reflection first. Component data goes through caffeine.component / caffeine_component_* , driven by the reflection registry, so new components are scriptable without new bindings. Messages stay the only editor mutation path. Scripts act on the play world, not on editor state. A feature is done when it has a test in both languages ( tests/test_script.cpp , tests/test_dryad_host.cpp ). 2. Parity matrix # Area Lua Dryad Lifecycle onCreate , onUpdate , onFixedUpdate yes yes onDestroy , onCollision , onPostProcess yes no Position and scale yes yes ( caffeine_get/set_position , scale, translate ) Generic components (reflection) yes yes Time ( delta , time , fixedDelta , scale, pause, frame) yes new ( caffeine_time_* ) Input (keys, axes, actions, mouse) yes new ( caffeine_input_* ) World create, destroy, alive, distance partly new ( caffeine_world_* ) Math: 2D and 3D vectors, scalar helpers new 3D Dryad stdlib Events, UI, draw2d, picking, assets, native modules yes no Post-process, animation, effects, navigation yes no 3. Added in this pass # Dryad natives # Native Returns caffeine_time_delta() , _u

Reference Last updated: 2026-11-18 Load native modules through the stable C ABI and expose them to Lua and Dryad. Caffeine can load game simulation libraries at play time. This is separate from Doppio editor plugins ( PluginAPI.hpp ). Layout # text Copy your-project/ native/ my_sim.so # Linux my_sim.dll # Windows Set the project search root via ScriptEngine::setSearchRoot (build output / project root). ABI (version 1) # Header: include/caffeine/runtime/NativeModuleAPI.h Required export: c Copy CAFFEINE_NATIVE_EXPORT const CaffeineNativeModuleInfo* caffeine_native_module_info ( void ) ; Optional exports: c Copy CAFFEINE_NATIVE_EXPORT void caffeine_native_on_load ( void * host_opaque) ; CAFFEINE_NATIVE_EXPORT void caffeine_native_on_unload ( void * host_opaque) ; CAFFEINE_NATIVE_EXPORT int caffeine_native_call ( const char * function, const char * args_json, char * out_buf, uint32_t out_capacity) ; caffeine_native_call returns 0 on success; non-zero on error (message in out_buf when possible). Arguments and results are UTF-8 JSON strings for portability. Lua # lua Copy caffeine.native. load ( "my_sim" ) local result = caffeine.native.call( "my_sim" , "step" , '{"dt":0.016}' ) Threading # Unless documented otherwise, native code runs on the main thread with the Lua VM and ECS. Do not call Lua from worker threads without synchronization. CI # Ship modules for each target platform; the engine does not cross-compile native code.

What is implemented # Kind Component Source Lua script ScriptComponent { scriptPath } .lua file, one environment per script path Dryad node script ScriptComponent with a .dyd path Node graph compiled and hosted by DryadHost Native script NativeScriptComponent C++ callbacks registered at runtime C++ script class CppScriptComponent CppScriptRegistry / CppScript Post-process driver PostProcessComponent + script onPostProcess(entityId, dt, api) , falls back to onUpdate The engine build enables scripting with CAFFEINE_ENABLE_SCRIPTING=ON (the default). For each entity with a script component it calls, when present: Hook When onCreate(entityId) First frame after the script is attached onUpdate(entityId, dt) Every scaled play-mode frame onFixedUpdate(entityId, dt) Fixed simulation step (default 60 Hz) onCollision(entityId, otherId) 2D physics collision onDestroy(entityId) Before the entity is destroyed onPostProcess(entityId, dt, api) Post-process driver; falls back to onUpdate Missing hooks are a no-op. This page documents the legacy terrain_plugin for the C++/ImGui host. The editor plugin that runs the Node.js terrain algorithm and imports the resulting heightmap into a TerrainComponent ; sculpting and painting stay in the engine. Type: editor plugin ( terrain_plugin.so ) Algorithm: assets/general-ultra-realistic-terrain-algorithm Services: terrain.generateUltra , terrain.importHeightmap Overview # The Terrain Generator plugin moves procedural generation out of the core. It uses the Node.js pipeline with domain warping and geomorphological PDEs (a more complete version than the old C++ generator removed from the engine). Flow: The user selects an entity with a TerrainComponent . Panel Terrain Generator → preset + world size + grid + seed. The plugin runs node caffeine-export.js in the algorithm directory. heightmap.txt + meta.json are imported via TerrainHeightmapImporter . TerrainCache rebuilds the render mesh, LOD and collision mesh. Editing is native. The Terrain Editor panel (sculpt, splat paint, undo and .cterrain I/O) is part of Caffeine core. This plugin only generates terrain procedurally and imports heightmaps; it registers a generator panel, not the terrain editor.
